hints.title: Annual Sales and Publication Window Filter
hints.text: Filter books available at least one month before 2019-06-23, then identify those with fewer than ten copies sold in the past year.

hints.title: Left Join with Date-Bounded Quantity Sum
hints.text: Left join books with orders dispatched between 2018-06-23 and 2019-06-23, grouping to test if total quantity is under ten.

hints.title: Unpopular Books Blueprint
hints.text: select b.book_id, b.name from Books b left join Orders o on b.book_id = o.book_id and o.dispatch_date between "2018-06-23" and "2019-06-23" where b.available_from <= "2019-05-23" group by b.book_id, b.name having coalesce(sum(o.quantity), 0) < 10.

hints.title: Complete Implementation
hints.text:
```mysql
SELECT b.book_id, b.name
FROM Books b
LEFT JOIN Orders o
  ON b.book_id = o.book_id
 AND o.dispatch_date BETWEEN '2018-06-23' AND '2019-06-23'
WHERE b.available_from <= '2019-05-23'
GROUP BY b.book_id, b.name
HAVING IFNULL(SUM(o.quantity), 0) < 10;
```

complexity.notes: Filtering on availability followed by hash-based left join aggregation runs in linear time.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Inner join ignores books with zero sales over the target year, misidentifying them as popular.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Condition in ON clause maintains books with zero sales without full outer table scans.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Correctly handling zero-sales books via LEFT JOIN and COALESCE / IFNULL.

SELECT b.book_id, b.name
FROM Books b
LEFT JOIN Orders o
  ON b.book_id = o.book_id
 AND o.dispatch_date BETWEEN '2018-06-23' AND '2019-06-23'
WHERE b.available_from <= '2019-05-23'
GROUP BY b.book_id, b.name
HAVING COALESCE(SUM(o.quantity), 0) < 10;

import pandas as pd

def unpopular_books(books: pd.DataFrame, orders: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    valid_books = books[books['available_from'] <= '2019-05-23']
    annual_orders = orders[(orders['dispatch_date'] >= '2018-06-23') & (orders['dispatch_date'] <= '2019-06-23')]
    sales = annual_orders.groupby('book_id')['quantity'].sum().reset_index()
    merged = valid_books.merge(sales, on='book_id', how='left')
    merged['quantity'] = merged['quantity'].fillna(0)
    res = merged[merged['quantity'] < 10]
    return res[['book_id', 'name']]
solutions.approach: Pandas Left Merge with Zero Quantity Fill
